assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn nucleobase deamination chemistry into a programmable tool for single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks. It is a clear, original chemical-biology invention with fast, broad use in research and in clinical translation. From a nucleotide-chemistry viewpoint it is among the cleanest cases of chemistry reshaping biology.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive conceptual and engineering advances; Komor (cytosine editors) and Gaudelli (adenine editors, which needed evolved deaminases acting on DNA) were the lead experimental inventors. This supports a coherent three-person prize. Kondo and Nishida's parallel cytidine-deaminase work is a priority-sharing question I would flag but not resolve.
assessment.maturity: Independent reproduction is extensive across many laboratories, organisms and early clinical programs, and the editing outcomes are measured quantitatively (efficiency, bystander edits, off-target deamination). Recognition is timely rather than premature, though long-term clinical safety is still maturing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prime-editing candidate (B011), which shares Liu and could draw the same prize slot.
Priority of the Kondo/Nishida parallel work, and how it should be weighed against the three-person limit.
Off-target deamination and long-term clinical safety data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis rests on reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry, fluorescent readout and polymerase enzymology. It transformed genomics, cancer biology and medicine, with a lasting impact on the whole field. It is a method built from a well-defined chemical reaction and is directly relevant to genome-maintenance research.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the single-molecule, reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry that became Solexa/Illumina. Other credited individuals (Rothberg for pyrosequencing-based platforms, Ju and Mayer for related chemistries) made real contributions to different platform lineages, so a two-person prize is defensible but requires deciding which lineage is core. My knowledge of the finer priority history is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: the technology has been in universal use for well over a decade, with overwhelming independent validation. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to separate the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry from the platform lineages that came from different groups.
Parts of the priority history across commercial platforms are not something I have independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders use small molecules to bring a target protein to an E3 ligase and so trigger its degradation. This is a new chemical modality that works catalytically and is already in clinical trials. The mechanism is well defined and gives biologists a general way to remove proteins acutely.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies carried out the original PROTAC concept and its early demonstrations; Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and degrader design made the approach drug-like. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim) is a distinct lineage, including the thalidomide mechanism, and could argue for a different configuration. I chose the PROTAC trio but accept that the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism and ternary-complex structure are confirmed by many independent groups, and several degraders are in clinical trials. No approved PROTAC yet, so clinical validation is still maturing.
uncertainties: Approved PROTAC drugs are still lacking, so clinical proof is incomplete.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be one prize or two lineages, and who is decisive in each.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative and large-scale mass-spectrometry proteomics made it possible to measure thousands of proteins, their modifications and their interactions, a capability biologists and biochemists now rely on. As a measurement-centered person, I value work that replaced assumptions with quantitative data. The impact is very broad and long-lasting.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, quantitative and SILAC-type proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative proteomics, SRM/SWATH) and Yates (shotgun proteomics, MudPIT) each made decisive, distinct contributions. Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also credited and plausible, so the three-person limit forces a difficult choice. The electrospray ionization foundation was recognized in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely reproduced and adopted. Recognition could be considered timely or overdue.
uncertainties: The three-person limit makes any selection contestable among Mann, Aebersold, Yates, Hunt, Gygi and others.
The overlap with the recognized electrospray and MALDI contributions may reduce the perceived novelty for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids with new chemical functionality into proteins. It is original and conceptually clear, and gave biologists a general tool and a route to new chemistry in living systems. It is a strong chemistry-of-life contribution.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established site-specific incorporation in E. coli and then in eukaryotic cells; Chin extended the work to multicellular organisms and to reprogramming the code, including orthogonal ribosomes and quadruplet codons. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed, but the trio above is the most natural. Credit is reasonably clear compared with many candidates.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and applied for two decades, with applications in protein therapeutics and imaging. Timely or somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from earlier directed-evolution and tRNA-engineering recognition.
The relative weight of the contributions of Mehl and Yokoyama is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that m6A is a reversible mRNA modification, with writers, erasers and readers, established an epitranscriptomic regulatory layer. It is a chemical modification turned into a regulatory system, with strong biological and disease relevance. I would weigh the evidence for specific mechanistic claims carefully.
assessment.attribution: Jia and He identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and proposed reversibility; Jaffrey, Rechavi and Dominissini mapped m6A transcriptome-wide (m6A-seq/MeRIP). Attribution between the reversibility discovery and the mapping work is distinct and not entirely resolved, so any three-person configuration is a judgment. I am not independently verifying the detailed priority history.
assessment.maturity: The field is large and reproducible in its core findings, but there have been disputes about specific details such as the physiological substrate of FTO, antibody specificity and quantification. This argues for a more cautious view of maturity.
uncertainties: Disputes about the FTO substrate and about the quantification and antibody specificity of m6A mapping.
Which of the reversibility and mapping contributions is decisive, and how to credit Jia, Dominissini and Meyer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal that many cellular compartments form by liquid-liquid phase separation changed how cell organization is understood, linking physical chemistry to cell biology. The idea is original and influential, including for neurodegeneration and cancer. I would still want to know how well specific cellular claims hold up under quantitative tests.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed liquid-like P granules, and Rosen's reconstitution with defined multivalent proteins gave a chemical-physical framework; Pappu and Mittag contributed to the theory and sequence determinants. Credit is plausible for a trio but contested at the edges.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing: many results come from overexpression or in vitro conditions, and there is active debate about what is truly phase-separated in cells at endogenous concentrations. I regard this as perhaps a bit early.
uncertainties: Controversy over whether in-cell condensates reflect equilibrium phase separation at physiological concentrations.
Boundary between physical-chemistry principles and descriptive cell biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant pocket, and the earlier chemical-genetic analog-sensitive kinase approach, turned a target long considered undruggable into one with approved drugs. The chemical principle is clear and the impact on cancer treatment is concrete. It is a good match for a committee valuing mechanism-level chemistry with biomedical relevance.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the clear single decisive contributor to the KRAS G12C covalent-ligand discovery and to chemical genetics of kinases, which makes a single-laureate configuration clean. Contributions from industry teams developing clinical inhibitors are not credited in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Approved KRAS G12C inhibitors confirm the approach clinically, and the structural basis is independently reproduced. Recognition looks timely, though durability of responses and resistance remain open.
uncertainties: Resistance to KRAS G12C inhibitors limits clinical durability.
The industrial drug-development teams that made the approved drugs are not part of the credit supplied here.
